extracted.intended_audience: legislators, Department of the Interior officials, tribal leaders, policy researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed administrative procedures for the Department of the Interior to follow when deciding whether to acknowledge the existence of certain Indian tribes, including testimony, bill text, and submitted principles for tribal credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish administrative procedure and guidelines (S.2375)
rubrics_metrics.description: Senate Bill 2375 establishes administrative procedure to be followed by the Department of the Interior in acknowledging a federal relationship with certain Indian tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hearing record includes the bill itself, proceedings, and witness statements — use S.2375's text as the proposed framework for DOI decisionmaking on acknowledgment (procedural steps, standards, and institutional responsibilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: NCAI's 12 principles for determining tribal credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Congress of American Indians (NCAI) submitted 12 principles for determining tribal credentials which, if incorporated in the bill, would make it acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 12 principles are presented as substantive criteria for evaluating petitions for recognition; they are intended to define credential thresholds and would be integrated into the administrative guideline language (the page notes their submission but does not enumerate them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid massive and indiscriminate recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Concern that massive and indiscriminate recognition of groups claiming to be tribes might result in the 'federal funding pie' being sliced too thin among beneficiary groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should consider fiscal/resource impacts and guard against overly broad or indiscriminate acknowledgments that would dilute federal benefits; weigh inclusion goals against resource allocation consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational placement of the recognition office
rubrics_metrics.description: Objection was raised to the proposed creation of a new office in the Department of the Interior to consider and process petitions for federal recognition; suggestion that such an office might instead be established within the existing framework of the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing administrative structures, consider avoiding unnecessary duplication of personnel and leveraging existing BIA expertise and institutional capacity; evaluate tradeoffs between a new standalone office and placement within BIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing overlooked tribes under Indian trust responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Over 100 of the nation's 400 Indian tribes are overlooked in the administration of Indian trust responsibility; S.2375 aims to acknowledge a federal relationship with certain tribes to remedy oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for recognition should include mechanisms to identify and remedy historical oversight, ensuring tribes previously overlooked by trust administration can be fairly considered for federal acknowledgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record completeness: include bill, proceedings, and witness statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The document includes the bill text, proceedings of the hearing, and informal and prepared statements of witnesses appearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative guideline development and evaluation should be informed by legislative text and the full record of testimony and stakeholder statements to capture policy intent, objections, and recommended criteria (e.g., NCAI principles).
